evidence.observation: `main` is the publisher entrypoint. It resolves --input, validates the local bundle via validateBundle(), builds the publication record and writes publication.json, then at lines 285-288 the `--dry-run` branch prints a confirmation and returns BEFORE the temporary directory / downloadIndex / uploadJson / aws spawnSync calls. Every S3 or network touch (aws at line 185, downloadIndex at 200/293, uploadJson at 215/314/320) is reachable only after that return, so --dry-run is a purely local, offline-safe validation of the fixture.

`parseArgs` recognizes the `--dry-run` flag (lines 47-50) and gates the credential/target requirements: `--bucket` and `--endpoint` are only mandatory when NOT dry-running (lines 68-69). This makes an offline run possible with neither an S3 bucket nor a network endpoint, i.e. operation against a fixture that intentionally carries no network configuration.

The `scripts` block defines the offline model-data toolchain: `check:model-data` (line 59) runs scripts/check-model-data.ts, which imports only node:fs-based local validators, and `build:offline` (line 61) composes `check:model-data` with the tsgo build while copying local src/providers/data into dist. `generate-model-catalog` (line 58) emits the ../../.artifacts/model-catalog input that scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs consumes. All three operate on checked-in local data with no network fetch, so this package's catalog pipeline is the offline fixture the publisher validates.

claims.claim: scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs supports a fully offline operation mode: with --dry-run it validates a local model-catalog fixture (500 chat + 1 image + 1 classifier models across 3 providers) and returns from main() before any aws/S3/network call, so the fixture never needs network data.

packages/ai/package.json defines the offline model-data scripts (check:model-data, build:offline, generate-model-catalog) that read only local checked-in data and produce the catalog input directory consumed by publish-model-catalog.mjs; no script in this pipeline performs a network fetch.

conclusion: The `pi` repository can be operated offline against its self-contained model-catalog fixture. The narrowest valid local check is the dry-run publisher test `node --test scripts/publish-model-catalog.test.mjs`, which builds a fixture in a temp dir and invokes `scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs --input <fixture> --source-commit test-commit --dry-run`. It passed with 1/1 tests green. The same dry-run was also run directly against .prale-eval/fixture, producing the normalized publication result (revision sha256-a9e95677...77918, providerCount 3, chatModelCount 500, imageModelCount 1, classifierModelCount 1, totalModelCount 502) with exit code 0 and the message 'no objects uploaded'. The check is offline-safe because --dry-run returns from main() at lines 285-288 before any aws spawnSync, downloadIndex, or uploadJson call; the only non-local helper gitSourceCommit() is bypassed by passing an explicit --source-commit, and the publisher imports solely node builtins plus the local ./model-catalog-protocol.ts.

validation.notes: Ran inside the workspace with Node v24.14.0 (native TypeScript type-stripping loads the local ./model-catalog-protocol.ts import). Result: 1 test, 1 pass, 0 fail. No node_modules are installed and none are required: the test and publisher use only node:assert, node:child_process, node:fs, node:os, node:path, node:crypto, node:util, node:test. Offline safety: the fixture is constructed in a tmpdir and passed with --dry-run, which short-circuits main() before every aws/S3 call site; --source-commit is supplied explicitly so the local git rev-parse helper is not invoked. An independent direct run `node scripts/publish-model-catalog.mjs --input .prale-eval/fixture --source-commit offline-fixture --dry-run` also exited 0 and wrote .prale-eval/operation-result.json. No network access, dependency install, or filesystem scan outside the workspace was performed.
